purpose: One setting inside a flush `Card`: an `Item` whose content carries the title and description, with the control placed by what it needs. A typed or picked field sits in a right cell capped at the 3xs container so every field on the card ends at the same edge (`field`); a switch or a button sits hard right at its natural width (`compact`); a textarea, list, radio group or editor drops under the copy at the full measure (`stacked`). A child setting indents one or two levels under a rule (`level`).
useWhen: Every row of a settings card: account settings, build settings, create pages, resource settings.
A field with a validation message under it (put the `HelperText` in the default slot after the control).
avoidWhen: A stand-alone form field with a visible label above it → use `field-text` and the other `field-*` components.
A read-only list of label and value pairs → use `key-value-pairs`.
A navigable list row → use `item` directly.
related: settings-section` — the band the card of rows sits in.
item` — the row primitive it renders; place rows in an `Item.List` inside the card.
helper-text` — the required or invalid message under the control.
bestPractices: The title is the label: give the control the same text as `aria-label`.
Pick `kind` by the control: `field` for Input and Select, `compact` for Switch and Button, `stacked` for Textarea, radio groups and editors.
Show a validation message only after Save was pressed.
Use `level` only for a setting that applies when the row above it is on, and render it with `v-if` on that state.
